title: Separate P104 causal hosted transfer from FutureAttr accounting
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

A synthetic Q96 word passes the complete 416-input native endpoint while the selected eight-port clique has causal public residual −I₈ and owned causal sum zero. Conservation attribution on the same execution assigns −I₈ to the owned lifetimes. A distinct finite control has a genuinely selected hot relay. The original #7113 source has a rank-two causal public residual, positive direct and hot contributions, and fails the selected GTD and cold hypotheses.

## Task and overlap

The word and path checks use #7113 at 07a76c5e2738882c0cb322278e56f6cae3c9885d and #7852 at 41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212. #7870 varies flux and grade in exact words. Here the question is whether causal transfer can replace FutureAttr weights in hM, including the public-helper bypass. The upstream #7869 guidance describes other rise classes.

## Validation and credit

The standalone exact trace.py and cf_review.py commands, source and manifest checks, positive hot-relay example and rejected bypass mutation are in the packet. The work was AI-assisted with Codex. Credit DreamingOfClouds, Rohan Arun and the original supplied word contributors.

## Open next questions

The conditional hM construction still needs a real FutureAttr-to-CFChain binding with hF, hG and billed lifetime costs. The synthetic bypass fails hG. No general rise or κ claim follows.
